entities.summary:
Silvio Passerini was an Italian cardinal born in the late 15th century. Born around 1495, he rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church to become a prominent figure in Renaissance Rome.

As Cardinal, Passerini played a key role in several high-profile diplomatic missions, including the negotiations leading up to the Council of Trent. He also served as an advisor to Pope Clement VII and was instrumental in shaping the Pope's foreign policy during the tumultuous years following Martin Luther's Reformation.

Despite his influential position, Passerini's life was marked by personal tragedy when he died on April 30, 1529, at the age of 34. His untimely passing left a void in the Church that would be felt for generations to come.

The legacy of Silvio Passerini can still be seen today in the many churches and institutions he helped build during his lifetime. His commitment to the Catholic faith and his role as a diplomat have made him an important figure in the history of Christianity.
